messages:
maria.support: @jonathan.dev FYI — we got a P1 from Acme this morning. Their function/tool calls are failing with "invalid tool args: failed to parse JSON". Root payload they sent below.

maria.support: Payload (as sent by customer):
```json
{"title": "Q1 planning", "start": "2025-03-10T09:00:00Z", "attendees": ["alice@example.com", "bob@example.com",], "metadata": "needs\"escape\""
}
```

maria.support: They say it used to work 2 days ago. They attached request_id=req_aa23b4. They tried SDK v1.4.2 and raw curl. Error from our API:
```
ERROR: tool_call_parse_error: invalid JSON at position 78: trailing comma
function: calendar.add_event
request_id=req_aa23b4
```

jonathan.dev: I can reproduce quickly. The payload has a trailing comma after bob@example.com and the closing brace newline mismatch. Looks like the customer's JS serializer sometimes leaves trailing commas in arrays when building strings manually. Also the metadata has an escaped quote which in bash gets eaten if wrapped in double quotes incorrectly.

akshay.sre: deploy-bot shows we rolled out a change to the function-caller on 2025-03-08 (deploy d1f3b2) that tightened JSON validation to strict RFC parsing. Previously we tolerated trailing commas. This likely explains the regression.

deploy-bot: Deploy d1f3b2 -> function-caller: "strict-json-parse" applied to prod on 2025-03-08 07:12 UTC :rocket:

jonathan.dev: Two options: ask the customer to fix their payload or add a tolerant path. Short-term, tell them to run `jq --compact-output` or use proper JSON serialization. Example curl that preserves escapes:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/call" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data-binary @payload.json
```
Where payload.json contains the valid JSON.

lizze.product: We should be careful — rolling back strict parsing reduces correctness for function schema enforcement. Could we add a transformation step: attempt a tolerant parse then strictly validate? Maybe behind a per-tenant flag.

maria.support: Customer asked for a hotfix. They're blocked in production; timeline is urgent. They specifically asked if we can accept trailing commas for function args again.

jonathan.dev: Short-term patch: modify parse path to try a tolerant parser (JSON5) on failure, then reserialize and validate against the function schema. I'll open a PR. Needs SRE signoff for risk. Patch idea:
```js
try { return JSON.parse(body) } catch(e) {
  // fallback to tolerant parser
  const o = JSON5.parse(body)
  return JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(o))
}
```

akshay.sre: Low risk but needs canary. I'll run a 30-minute canary on 5% traffic. If green, we can promote to more traffic.

jonathan.dev: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/function-caller/pull/842 (WIP) — includes fallback to JSON5 and tests. Added logging for original_payload_snippet (truncated to 1k chars, PII-safe). Tests cover trailing commas, single quotes, and escaped quotes.

maria.support: Customer accepted the workaround for now (they'll sanitize on their side) but requested an ETA for the hotfix. Can we target a patch today?

akshay.sre: If canary passes, we can promote within ~6 hours. Scheduling canary now.

deploy-bot: Canary started on prod-rack-3 (5% traffic). Monitor: https://ops.redwood.ai/canaries/842

jonathan.dev: Noted. I'll follow up after canary metrics. Also added a health check for function-caller to fail fast if JSON5 parsing produces unexpected types.

lizze.product: Please document the customer workaround in Support KB: "Function calls failing with JSON parse errors — escaping and trailing commas". Assign to maria.support to draft.

maria.support: Will draft KB and loop legal if we include log snippets. ETA 4 hours. :thumbsup:

jonathan.dev: ETA for PR -> deploy if canary ok: ~4-6 hours. I'll include a toggle to disable tolerant parsing per-tenant.

maria.support: Closing loop with customer once patch deployed. Adding to postmortem if rollback needed. Thanks team :heart:
